candidate.falsifier: A nonpositive direct witness row kills this far-lift direct checkpoint. A larger adverse z-score kills the narrower below-3 finite cap and forces a looser or arithmetic concentration target.
candidate.mechanism: Reuse the stressed positive-pushback residue classes, but lift them beyond the previous variance-scale holdout and measure the same explicit four-modulus coefficient function against local variance and actual strict-central pair count.
candidate.name: four-modulus variance-scale far-lift stress holdout
candidate.prediction: If the variance-scale route is portable, the direct witness should remain positive and adverse z-scores should stay moderate on the farther lifts. A fixed below-3 cap is a separate finite subclaim and can fail without killing direct positivity.
candidate.smallest_test: Take the same 29 source residue classes and evaluate their next four period-lifts after the prior 116-row holdout.

decision: The farther targeted lift preserves direct four-modulus positivity on every checked row, but it falsifies the narrower finite subclaim that adverse iid-scale z stays below 3.  The variance-scale route remains live only as a looser signed concentration/equidistribution target tied to local main-term positivity, not as a fixed three-sigma cap.  Residual absorption constants remain finite fits only, and Goldbach remains open.
status_boundary: finite q286-WBSS four-modulus far-lift holdout only; no independence theorem, fixed-modulus equidistribution theorem, q286 threshold theorem, strict-central Goldbach theorem, or Goldbach proof
